data.blog_title: What’s new in Fabric Eventstream: July–December 2025 updates
data.feature_description: ### Large Message Support in Fabric Eventstreams  #### Overview  Large Message Support enables Fabric Eventstreams to ingest, process, and deliver event payloads up to **20 MB** per message. This removes the need for customers to split, chunk, or pre-process large events before streaming them through Eventstreams.  #### Problem  Today, Eventstreams enforces a default message size limit of 1 MB. Customers with larger payloads -- such as batched IoT telemetry, enriched event schemas, media metadata, or complex domain events -- must implement workarounds to stay within this constraint. These workarounds add pipeline complexity, increase failure surface, and break downstream schema consistency.  #### What's changing  With this feature, customers can opt in to a configurable message size ceiling (up to 20 MB) on their Eventstreams. Key aspects:  - **Opt-in by design** -- existing Eventstreams are unaffected unless the customer explicitly enables a higher limit. - **Configurable ceiling** -- customers choose the maximum message size aligned to their workload, rather than a one-size-fits-all default. - **No pipeline redesign required** -- sources, transformations, and destinations continue to work as expected. Larger messages flow through the same Eventstream canvas.
data.feature_name: Large message support ( 20 MB) for Fabric Event streams

data.blog_title: Empowering Real-Time Searches: Vector Similarity Search with Eventhouse
data.feature_description: # Generally Available: Vector Search and Vector Indexes in Azure SQL Vector Search and Vector Indexes are now generally available in Azure SQL Database. Using the [CREATE VECTOR INDEX](https://learn.microsoft.com/sql/t-sql/statements/create-vector-index-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver17) and [VECTOR_SEARCH](https://learn.microsoft.com/sql/t-sql/functions/vector-search-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver17) T-SQL capabilities, you can perform efficient approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) searches for AI scenarios such as semantic search, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), recommendation systems, and image search. Built on the DiskANN algorithm, Vector Indexes enable efficient vector similarity search over large datasets while allowing you to combine vector search with relational queries and filtering directly in Azure SQL Database.By bringing AI retrieval directly into Azure SQL Database, you can build AI-powered applications on your enterprise data without requiring a separate vector database, simplifying application architecture while leveraging the reliability, security, and governance capabilities of Azure SQL Database.**Learn more:** [Vector Search & Vector Indexes documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/sql/sql-server/ai/vectors?view=sql-server-ver17)

data.feature_description: Microsoft Fabric Runtime 2.1 updates the Apache Spark foundation to Spark 4.2 and Delta Lake 4.4, with Python 3.14, Scala 2.13, and Java 21. For supported workloads, the Native Execution Engine is enabled by default to provide acceleration without extra configuration, while documented opt-out and controlled fallback paths preserve compatibility.Runtime 2.1 also introduces a leaner built-in package baseline with PySpark and SparkR. Customers can add compatible optional Python and R libraries through Library Manager or a Fabric Environment, reducing package conflicts while preserving flexibility for data engineering and data science workloads. The Public Preview is targeted for January 31, 2027 and includes migration guidance, known limitations, and preview support information.
data.feature_name: Runtime 2.1 (Spark 4.2 and Delta 4.4)

data.blog_title: Enhanced Monitoring for Spark High Concurrency Workloads in Microsoft Fabric
data.feature_description: This feature delivers a comprehensive Notebook Run Lineage experience for Spark applications, enabling data engineers to monitor and analyze complex notebook workflows with ease. It provides an at-a-glance view of all notebook run statuses, helps quickly identify root-cause failures across nested executions, and highlights performance bottlenecks. Users can filter and explore large execution graphs, access detailed error and run-level information, and view aggregated summaries of execution health and resource usage--all in one place.
data.feature_name: Track and Manage Notebook Run Dependencies & Linage View

data.feature_description: Fuzzy string matching - Use fuzzy, or approximate, string matching to check if two strings are similar, and calculate the difference between two strings. Use this capability to identify strings that might be different because of character corruption. Corruption includes spelling errors, transposed characters, missing characters, or abbreviations. Fuzzy string matching uses algorithms to detect similar sounding strings.
data.feature_name: Fuzzy String Match

data.blog_title: Extracting deeper insights with Fabric Data Agents in Copilot in Power BI
data.feature_description: # Microsoft Copilot Integrated into Power BI and Microsoft FabricCopilot experiences have emerged across the applications people use every day, bringing AI closer to the work happening in each product. But this can also feel fragmented, with different entry points, separate conversations, and uncertainty about which Copilot agent to use.Our goal is to create a consistent Copilot experience that is available wherever people work. No one should have to leave the application they are using to find it. Microsoft Copilot should come into their experience, carry context with them, and connect to the specialized intelligence of each product.  This release will allow tenant admins the opportunity to choose Microsoft Copilot as an alternative to the Power BI standalone Copilot experience, bringing all of M365 into Power BI for licensed users.## One Familiar Place for Context and Trusted DataThis integration gives users one familiar place to bring together business context and trusted data. Shared conversation history lets them continue a discussion as they move between Microsoft Copilot experiences instead of starting over in each application.For someone starting in Power BI, a question no longer has to stop with the numbers in a report. A sales leader could use **Fabric IQ** to identify which regions are behind plan, then use **Work IQ** to connect the results with customer emails, meetings, account plans, and documents.They could summarize the complete picture and even kick off actions and tasks in **Cowork**, all from inside Power BI. This work context and ability to move directly from insight to action were not available in the standalone Power BI Copilot experience.## Administrator ControlsA new setting in the Fabric admin portal will determine whether this integration is available by enabling or disabling the entry point in the navigation pane.The setting will be **off by default**, giving administrators time to evaluate the experience before introducing it to their organization. Administrators can enable it when they are ready and disable it if they need to pause access.This setting is independent of the existing setting for standalone Power BI Copilot:- If both settings are enabled, users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license will see entry points for both experiences. Standalone Power BI Copilot will continue to appear on Home.- If standalone Power BI Copilot is disabled and Microsoft 365 Copilot is enabled, users will see only the Microsoft 365 Copilot entry point.## Initial Public Preview AvailabilityDuring the initial public preview, the integrated experience is available only to users with a **Microsoft 365 Copilot license**.These users receive the full Copilot Chat experience in Power BI and Fabric, bringing together:- Fabric data through **Fabric IQ**- Relevant Microsoft 365 context through **Work IQ**Existing permissions and governance controls continue to determine which content each user can access.
data.feature_name: Copilot in Power BI Fabric

data.blog_title: Service Principal Support for Data Agents in Fabric (Preview)
data.feature_description: Fabric Data Agent supports service principal (SPN) authentication, enabling agent-to-agent scenarios such as Microsoft Foundry calling a Data Agent using an SPN. However, SPN-based access is not currently supported with Row-Level Security (RLS). Supporting SPN + RLS would allow the Data Agent to preserve the appropriate user-level data permissions while using an SPN for service-to-service authentication, enabling more secure and flexible enterprise scenarios where both application identity and user identity need to be respected.
data.feature_name: Support SPN + RLS

data.blog_title: Surge protection gets smarter: introducing workspace-level controls (Preview)
data.feature_description: Workspace-level surge protection helps capacity administrators prevent a single workspace from unexpectedly consuming an entire capacity. Administrators can set workspace consumption limits, exempt mission-critical workspaces, and block or unblock workspaces to maintain capacity health and quality of service.  There will also be an API that supports these actions alongside an API for the existing Capacity-level Surge Protection feature as part of this release.  Finally, there will be the ability to opt-in to notifications via email - and see them in product - when a surge protection activity occurs.
data.feature_name: Surge Protection V2 (Workspace-level)

data.blog_title: Introducing capacity overage: Flexibility when you need it most (Preview)
data.feature_description: Fabric capacity overage is an opt-in feature in Microsoft Fabric that automatically bills for excess capacity usage in a pay-as-you-go basis instead of throttling operations - enabling capacity administrators to protect capacities from being throttled.  Today, as a capcity admin, you can use surge protection, resize capacities, or pay for dedicated capacities to try to protect mission critical jobs, but all these approaches still can result in throttling and rejection due to insufficient provisioned capacity.  Overage billing addresses this consideration.  The solution allows a capacity admin to opt-in to paying off their smoothed usage and overages instead of being throttled.As Microsoft releases Fabric Overage Billing the Capacity Metrics App will be updated to reflect this new capability.  Specifically, views this will include clear visibility into overage events, showing when Overage Billing was activated and overage charges are being assessed - as well as cases where the capacity is reaching the overage billing limits set and is experiencing throttling.  The view also will show trends over time alongside the amount of utilization.  These enhancements, alongside the core Overage Billing capability, make it easier to monitor costs, optimize resource allocation, and ensure business continuity through flexible capacity management capabilities.  There will also be a new ARM API for Capacity Creation that supports Capacity Overage.  There will also be an ability, both as opt-in emails and in-product, to receive notifications when overage activity occurs or subsides.
data.feature_name: Fabric Capacity Overage

data.blog_title: Providing more insights & tools: Capacity health, timepoint summary, timepoint detail, chargeback now generally available
data.feature_description: The Capacity Metrics app will features a redesigned experience with modernized visualizations, improved navigation, and enhanced analytics capabilities that make it easier to monitor, understand, and optimize Microsoft Fabric capacity usage.The updated experience provides clearer insights into utilization trends, workload consumption patterns, and performance bottlenecks, helping administrators more quickly identify capacity constraints, investigate throttling events, and make data-driven decisions to improve capacity health and efficiency.
data.feature_name: Capacity Metrics app

data.blog_title: Customer-managed keys for Fabric workspaces (Generally Available)
data.feature_description: Apply Fabric workspace customer managed keys to Eventstreams to add an extra layer of encryption for data at rest. When CMK is enabled for a workspace, Eventstreams automatically use the workspace key configuration via Azure Key Vault, including key rotation and revocation handling.
data.feature_name: Secure Fabric Eventstreams with customer-managed keys

data.blog_title: Capacity Overview Events in Real-Time Hub (Generally Available)
data.feature_description: **Capacity Monitoring in Monitor Hub **Microsoft Fabric is introducing capacity monitoring and management capabilities within the Fabric product itself, designed to give administrators a unified and actionable view of capacity health, usage, and management capabilities. This experience centralizes the most critical controls and insights--such as around utilization, scaling, throttling, and surge protection--making it easier than ever to detect issues, manage resources, and remediate capacities quickly.  Key initials features include CU utilization details with breakdowns (e.g., interactive/background delays and rejections), status indicators for surge protection and throttling, direct toggles for pausing or resuming capacities, and easy ways to take direct actions for unhealthy capacities such scaling capacities and/or performing workspace migrations right from within the experience.By bringing these capabilities into the Monitor Hub, Fabric empowers customers to proactively manage capacities, maintain reliability, and streamline operations--all from an intuitive interface that introduces the concept of Capacity Health.
data.feature_name: Capacity Insights & Actions (in-product observability)

data.blog_title: Providing more insights & tools: Capacity health, timepoint summary, timepoint detail, chargeback now generally available
data.feature_description: **Fabric Chargeback app - Tags Support **Chargeback app tagging will enable organizations to attribute and analyze capacity consumption across customer-defined business dimensions such as project, function, workspace, cost center, or department. This enhancement will provide greater flexibility for cost allocation, chargeback, and reporting scenarios, helping customers align Fabric consumption with their internal financial and organizational structures.About the app:  The** Microsoft Fabric Chargeback app** helps customers understand which teams, users, and workloads are driving capacity usage, enabling them to build chargeback processes that fairly allocate costs based on actual consumption. As a capacity admin, you can view key parameters such as metric types, dates, and operation names, and share the report with others in your organization to support transparent and informed cost management.  Ultimately, this enables admins to:* Understand cost drivers - See which workspaces, users, or artifacts consume the most resources.* Enable accurate chargeback - Distribute costs fairly across departments based on real usage.* Optimize capacity planning - Identify expensive artifacts and adjust capacity assignments or auto-scale settings to control costs.With these insights, admins can make informed decisions about capacity sizing, workload distribution, and budgeting/chargeback--ensuring cost transparency and operational efficiency.
data.feature_name: Fabric Chargeback app

data.blog_title: Introducing Migration assistant for SQL database in Fabric (Preview)
data.feature_description: Fabric Migration Assistant for SQL Database is Generally Available
data.feature_name: Fabric SQL | SQL Server migration to Fabric SQL | GA

data.blog_title: Capacity Operation Events in Real-Time Hub (Preview)
data.feature_description: Capacity Operation Events in Real-Time Hub provide Microsoft Fabric capacity administrators with near-real-time, operation-level telemetry for understanding exactly what is consuming capacity and contributing to performance pressure.- The event stream emits one event for each operation that consumes capacity units, rather than aggregating activity into a summary window.- Each event can include the operation's workspace, item, workload, identity, CU consumption, duration, status, throttling delay, start time, and smoothing-window attribution.- Administrators can identify high-cost operations, investigate throttled or failed workloads, and determine which workspaces and items are driving capacity utilization.- Events can power Activator alerts and automated responses, flow through Eventstream to downstream destinations, be retained in Eventhouse for historical analysis, and support custom monitoring and governance solutions.- Used with Capacity Overview Events, administrators can move from understanding what is happening to the capacity to identifying which operations are causing it.This capability is available in public preview. Customers can access it from Real-Time Hub under Fabric events, then explore Capacity operation events, create an eventstream, or configure an alert for a selected capacity.
data.feature_name: Capacity Operation Events in Real-Time Hub (Public Preview)

data.blog_title: Capacity Overview Events in Real-Time Hub (Generally Available)
data.feature_description: Capacity Overview Events in Real-Time Hub give Microsoft Fabric capacity administrators a production-ready, near-real-time way to monitor capacity health and respond before users are affected.- Capacity Summary events are emitted every 30 seconds and provide a high-level view of capacity utilization and health across workloads, including CU consumption, overage, and throttling indicators.- Capacity State events are emitted when important conditions change, including when a capacity is paused, resumed, overloaded, or enters a throttling-related state.- Administrators can create Activator alerts and notifications, trigger automated operational workflows, route events through Eventstream, retain them in Eventhouse for historical analysis, and build custom monitoring experiences.- The generally available release includes the reliability, scalability, architecture, and monitoring improvements needed for production adoption.Together, these event streams help organizations detect capacity pressure earlier, automate responses, preserve operational history, and use trend data for governance and capacity planning. Customers can get started in Real-Time Hub by selecting Fabric events and Capacity overview events, then creating an eventstream or setting an alert for a selected capacity.
data.feature_name: Capacity Overview Events in Real-Time Hub (Generally Available)

data.blog_title: Outbound access protection for Data Factory (Generally Available)
data.feature_description: Workspace admins responsible for safeguarding organizational data will be able to leverage Outbound Access Control (OAP) in Fabric to ensure that Semantic Models and Power BI Reports are permitted to connect only to explicitly approved data sources. OAP helps to prevent data exfiltration by blocking data connections to unapproved or potentially risky endpoints, thereby enforcing organizational data governance and compliance requirements.
data.feature_name: Outbound access protection for Power BI (Reports)

data.blog_title: Supercharge Your Workflow: New Multitasking Features Coming to Fabric (Preview)
data.feature_description: We're improving Fabric's multitasking experience by giving users control over how context behaves when they open Fabric in another browser tab. Today, open items, tab order, pinned items, and tab groups automatically carry over to additional tabs in the same browser profile. While this supports continuity and multitasking, customer feedback indicates that some users prefer a clean workspace for separate tasks and that inherited items can contribute to reaching the 20-open-item limit.We're planning a user-selectable setting that lets users choose whether a new Fabric browser tab continues their existing context or opens with a clean context
data.feature_name: Enable/disable Fabric multitasking context carry across browser tabs

data.blog_title: AI-powered troubleshooting for Fabric pipeline error messages
data.feature_description: Copilot helps to troubleshoot Copy job error messages by providing clearer summary and actionable recommendations.
data.feature_name: Copy job - AI-powered Error Assistant and Insight for Copy Job

data.blog_title: Large string and binary values in Fabric Data Warehouse and SQL analytics endpoint for mirrored items (Generally Available)
data.feature_description: SQL analytics endpoints for Lakehouses will support large string and binary data using VARCHAR(MAX) and VARBINARY(MAX) types, up to 16 MB, with the new Metadata Sync feature.
data.feature_name: VARCHAR(MAX) support in SQL analytics endpoint of Lakehouses

data.blog_title: Easily load Fabric OneLake data into Excel — OneLake catalog and Get Data are integrated into Excel for Windows (Preview)
data.feature_description: The OneLake catalog integration in Excel as part of modern Get Data unlocks seamless connectivity to Fabric data, empowering every business user to discover and analyze organizational content directly from Excel. This powerful capability simplifies data access and accelerates insights, making Excel a true gateway to Fabric's rich data ecosystem.
data.feature_name: Fabric OneLake catalog in Excel Get Data

data.blog_title: Discover items across workspaces with the OneLake Catalog Search API, MCP and CLI tools (Preview)
data.feature_description: The OneLake Catalog Search API (POST /v1/catalog/search) -- previously limited to Fabric items -- now also returns OneLake tables (e.g. Lakehouse, Mirrored) and Semantic Model tables as first-class search results. Items and tables are ranked together in a single, unified relevance-scored result set -- so the most relevant result surfaces first regardless of entity type.
data.feature_name: OneLake catalog Search API expansion to OneLake and Semantic model tables

data.blog_title: Lineage-aware AI with the Fabric item relations API (Preview)
data.feature_description: Query upstream and downstream item relationships across all Fabric workloads through a public API. Retrieve which items depend on or feed into a given item, spanning Lakehouses, Warehouses, Pipelines, Semantic Models, Reports and more.
data.feature_name: Query item downstream and upstream relations through a public API

data.feature_description: External Changes Reload enables Power BI Desktop to automatically detect and apply changes made to PBIP project files by external tools such as Visual Studio Code, without requiring users to restart Power BI Desktop.
data.feature_name: Developer mode (PBIP) external changes reload

data.feature_description: The new Report Ribbon on the web brings the familiar Power BI Desktop ribbon experience to the browser, providing a more intuitive, organized, and consistent way to access report actions and authoring capabilities.
data.feature_name: Report Ribbon in the web

data.feature_description: We are bringing TMDL View in the web
data.feature_name: TMDL View in the Web

data.feature_description: Data Agent automatically follows the foreign key relationships in your SQL source to query the right tables -- including ones you didn't explicitly select. When you scope an agent to a schema or just a couple of base tables, the agent expands along those foreign keys to bring in the other tables a question needs and generates SQL that joins them correctly, so you get accurate multi-table answers from a small starting selection. For relationships that aren't defined in the source or live only in how your business uses the data, creators and advanced users can define additional relationships through the SDK & Data Agent experience. These configurations are stored alongside the rest of the agent configuration in a consistent, source-controllable format -- so they flow through your CI/CD pipeline
data.feature_name: Relationship Context for SQL Sources

data.blog_title: Build agent with AI for Data Agent (Preview)
data.feature_description: Advanced NL2SQL delivers more accurate and reliable query generation for SQL data sources by combining stronger data exploration, schema understanding, and example-driven reasoning. The agent is better at learning from example queries and applying those patterns to new user questions, even when requests have not been explicitly anticipated. Before generating queries, it can examine datasets, tables, columns, and relationships to identify the most relevant data and construct higher-quality queries with fewer instructions and less manual tuning. These enhancements improve first-pass query accuracy, reduce prompt engineering requirements, and enable Data Agents to answer a broader range of business questions with greater consistency and confidence.Today, these capabilities are available in preview through the [Preview Runtime](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/data-science/data-agent-runtime), which includes Advanced NL2SQL improvements such as better example query following, improved filter value substitution, and more effective ambiguity handling before generating queries. These capabilities will be generally available as part of the Advanced NL2SQL experience.
data.feature_name: Advanced NL2SQL Agent (General Availability)

data.feature_description: Query Templates are parameterized example queries for SQL databases and Semantic Models that teach Data Agents how to answer common business questions. By providing trusted query patterns with reusable parameters, Query Templates help agents generate more accurate and efficient queries, reducing ambiguity and improving consistency. Templates can be created manually, generated with AI, or built through a guided skill experience. By leveraging optimized query patterns, Data Agents can deliver faster responses, higher answer accuracy, and more reliable results while reducing the need for complex prompt engineering and extensive agent instructions.
data.feature_name: Parameterized Example Queries

data.blog_title: Public APIs – bulk import and export items definition (Preview)
data.feature_description: Import and export item definitions in bulk through a single API call. Enables workspace-as-code workflows, simplifies CI/CD pipelines, and accelerates cross-workspace migrations by eliminating the need to handle items one at a time.
data.feature_name: Bulk import and export item definition API

data.blog_title: Capacity Overview Events in Real-Time Hub (Generally Available)
data.feature_description: General availability of Capacity Overview events for monitoring Fabric capacity state changes via Azure and Fabric Events.
data.feature_name: Capacity Overview Events

data.feature_description: The Data Source schema description feature allows users to add rich descriptions to tables, columns, and other schema elements to enhance how the Data Agent understands and utilizes the data. These annotations provide valuable context that can improve routing decisions, schema selection, and query generation. By supplementing raw schema with user-defined descriptions--such as definitions, usage notes, or expected value formats--the agent can interpret questions more accurately and choose the most relevant data sources and fields when responding to user queries.
data.feature_name: Data Agent Schema Descriptions for SQL

data.blog_title: Data source routing in Microsoft Fabric data agents (Generally Available)
data.feature_description: The Routing Tool is a fallback mechanism used by the Data Agent to intelligently determine which tool or data source should handle a user's natural language query. When schema descriptions are available--either user-supplied or imported--they enhance the routing process by providing semantic context about each table or schema element. This context helps the agent make more accurate decisions about which tool (e.g., SQL, KQL) or dataset is best suited to answer the question. The routing tool activates when a query is ambiguous, ensuring queries are directed efficiently and appropriately. The routing tool results can be viewed by the creator for easier debugging.
data.feature_name: Improve Data Agent Data Source Selection Results

data.blog_title: IDENTITY columns support for Identity Insert (Generally Available)
data.feature_description: Identity columns are numeric columns that automatically increment with each new row value that is inserted into a table with an Identity column defined.
data.feature_name: Identity columns

data.blog_title: Simplifying Data Ingestion with Copy job – Introducing Change Data Capture (CDC) Support (Preview)
data.feature_description: With the PostgreSQL CDC connector in Copy job, you can capture inserts, updates, and deletes from PostgreSQL and copy them to any supported destination.
data.feature_name: Copy job - CDC based replication from PostgreSQL

data.blog_title: Simplifying Data Ingestion with Copy job – Introducing Change Data Capture (CDC) Support (Preview)
data.feature_description: With the MySQL CDC connector in Copy job, you can capture inserts, updates, and deletes from MySQL and copy them to any supported destination.
data.feature_name: Copy job - CDC based replication from MySQL

data.blog_title: Simplify your data movement with Copy job: CDC with SQL estate (Generally Available)
data.feature_description: Copy job provides a Salesforce CDC connector, allowing you to capture row-level inserts, updates, and deletes from Salesforce and replicate them to any supported destination.
data.feature_name: Copy job - CDC based replication from Salesforce

data.feature_description: To enhance security, we aim to prevent the sharing of Microsoft account credentials across collaborators. The new connection-sharing model will encourage each collaborator to sign in with their own Microsoft account.
data.feature_name: Connections - Enhanced Connection Collaboration Model

data.blog_title: Dataflow Gen2 and Power Query innovations at Microsoft Build: Low-code data transformation with standout scale, performance, and reuse
data.feature_description: Mapping Data Flows transformations will become generally available in Dataflow Gen2, bringing the proven, low-code, Spark-based transformation capabilities of Azure Data Factory and Azure Synapse directly into Microsoft Fabric.With this release, customers will be able to confidently author and run complex, large-scale data transformations using the same visual, code-free experience they rely on today--natively integrated into the Fabric Dataflow Gen2 experience and ready for business-critical workloads.This capability will unlock the full power of Mapping Data Flows within Fabric, delivering Spark-optimized execution with predictable performance at scale. Data engineers and analytics teams will be able to leverage advanced transformation patterns while working within a unified Fabric Data Factory environment, reducing operational overhead and eliminating the need to manage separate tools.Just as importantly, general availability of Mapping Data Flows in Dataflow Gen2 will provide a production-ready migration path for existing Azure Data Factory and Synapse customers. Teams will be able to move their existing Mapping Data Flow assets into Fabric with minimal rework, preserving investments in transformation logic while modernizing and standardizing their data integration architecture on Microsoft Fabric.
data.feature_name: Dataflows - Support for Mapping Data Flow transformations in Dataflow Gen2

data.blog_title: New Dataflow Gen2 data destinations and experience improvements
data.feature_description: We are introducing Amazon S3 as a new data destination for Dataflow Gen2 in Preview, enabling customers to publish transformed data from Microsoft Fabric directly into Amazon S3 using Dataflow Gen2's low-code Power Query experience.This preview expands Dataflow Gen2's destination ecosystem to better support multi-cloud data architectures, making it easier for customers with existing AWS investments to integrate Fabric-based transformations into their broader data lake and analytics environments.Key benefits and scenarios:* Publish curated outputs from Dataflow Gen2 directly to Amazon S3 buckets* Support AWS-based data lake and downstream analytics scenarios while keeping transformation logic centralized in Fabric* Enable teams to prepare, standardize, and shape data in Fabric before making it available to AWS services such as Athena, Glue, or other S3-based processing pipelinesDuring Preview, the Amazon S3 data destination is intended for evaluation and early adoption, allowing customers to validate cross-cloud integration patterns, performance characteristics, and operational workflows before using it for business-critical pipelines.This preview is part of our broader effort to make Dataflow Gen2 a flexible, low-code transformation layer across clouds, with continued investments planned to mature and expand multi-cloud destination support in Microsoft Fabric.
data.feature_name: Dataflows - New Data Destination: AWS S3

data.blog_title: Soft delete for On-premises data gateways in Microsoft Fabric (Preview)
data.feature_description: We are introducing user-facing soft delete for on-premises data gateways, giving administrators a safety net when gateways are removed.Accidental or premature deletion of a gateway can disrupt data refreshes and reports. With this update, administrators can:- Recover recently deleted gateways within a retention window.- Restore gateway configurations without recreating them from scratch.- Reduce the impact of accidental deletions on business-critical connectivity.This helps organizations protect against accidental loss of gateway configurations and maintain continuity.
data.feature_name: Gateways - Soft delete for gateways

data.blog_title: Automate your CI/CD pipelines with Microsoft Fabric Git REST APIs
data.feature_description: Commit individual files within a supported Fabric item to Git, rather than committing the entire item at once. File-level commits give developers granular change history, support partial commits of in-progress work, and produce smaller, easier-to-review pull requests.
data.feature_name: Git Integration - File level commit

data.blog_title: Incremental copy gets more flexible: New watermark column types in Copy job in Fabric Data Factory (Generally Available)
data.feature_description: Incremental copy from Copy job will support composite watermark columns for complex change detection, including scenarios where the maximum watermark is derived from multiple incremental columns such as LastCreateDateTime and LastModifiedDateTime together.
data.feature_name: Copy job - Support composite watermark columns for incremental copy

data.blog_title: Introducing New Branching Capabilities in Fabric Git Integration
data.feature_description: Branch workspace admin profile (aka. admin delegation) lets developers use the branch-out experience without needing create-workspace or assign-capacity permissions. Workspace admins keep full control through pre-configured guardrails while unblocking developer workflows. Capabilities:  - Developers without create-workspace or assign-capacity permissions can perform branch-out seamlessly  - Admins pre-configure profile to ensure guardrails for branch workspaces: developer role, capacity assignment and admin list.
data.feature_name: Git Integration - Branch workspace admin profile

data.blog_title: Introducing new Git developer experiences in Microsoft Fabric (Preview)
data.feature_description: When developers want to sync their workspace with the git repo, they want to view the changes made before taking actions.With this feature we will enable viewing the exact changes since the last sync between the workspace and the branch, as well as where those changes are.It will be shown as code compare experience that is familiar to developers. Devs can see what items and files have been changed, see the exact code changes and whether it is in a Fabric workspace, or in the repo.
data.feature_name: Git integration - compare code changes
